result:
Round 110 is done and waiting for C: the library's ◀, ▶ and × buttons no longer drop keyboard focus to the page body. The code-reviewer also raised a related focus bug that this fix does not cover. I reproduced it in Chromium and it goes to B as a new Medium finding. All my local checks pass, I only marked the acceptance criteria I actually ran, and the backlog item stays open until C passes it.

**What changed:** the repository ends with exactly the four allowed paths (2 modified, 2 new), and the frozen list still checks 544/544. No protected file was touched, and no server was started or stopped. Class strings, labels, titles and `data-testid`s are unchanged.
- `ArrangementLibrary.tsx`: when ◀ or ▶ is clicked while it has focus, the other one receives focus once it appears. This only happens if focus is still on the body or nowhere, so it never takes focus another component has moved. A × click that had focus sends focus to the search input. All three buttons ignore a held Enter's repeated keydowns, so ◀ and ▶ can't flip back and forth. No new state was added, so the render count is unchanged.
- `library-focus-handoff.test.tsx` (new, 13 tests). LF4 counts clips through the context and `[data-clip-id]`. LF0 first proves that Enter on the body really adds a clip, so the other tests can fail.
- Doc 095 (new). In doc 094, only line 4 changed: round 109 is C PASS and published in `1fe3ba2`.

**One change from D-29z75 for B to approve:** the handoff uses `focus({ preventScroll: true })` instead of plain `focus()`. The reviewer suspected plain `focus()` would scroll the library sideways, and Chromium confirmed it: after Enter on ▶ the panel was scrolled 243 px at the start of the opening animation and stayed off by 1 px at the end. With the fix it stays at 0 throughout. LF11 checks this.

**Checks I ran:**
- **Fail-before** (against B's snapshot, in a scratch copy): LF1, LF2, LF3, LF4, LF8, LF9, LF10 and LF11 fail; LF0, LF5, LF5b, LF6 and LF7 pass. This matches B's expectation; LF10 and LF11 were added after the review.
- **Mutations** (unchanged code passes 13/13 before and after):

  | Mutation | Tests that fail |
  |---|---|
  | m1: no handoff | LF1, LF2, LF3, LF4, LF9, LF10, LF11 |
  | m2: arm without checking focus | LF5b |
  | m3: drop the body/nothing-focused check | LF7 |
  | m4: no repeat guard on ◀/▶ | LF8, LF9 |
  | m5: wrong partner | LF1, LF4, LF9, LF10, LF11 |
  | m6: no `preventScroll` | LF11 |

- **typecheck:** passes.
- **lint:** 0 diagnostics in my files (218 warnings repo-wide, all in other files).
- **Biome:** clean on the two code files, without `--write`.
- **Targeted vitest:** 13 files, 309 tests, all pass. The grep found 12 files; I added `self-disabling-focus.test.tsx` by hand.
- **Not run:** the full suite, `verify` and the build, which belong to the gate.
- **Browser self-check** (Chromium, 1280; my evidence, not C's acceptance):
  - B's probe passes for all three buttons: after the first Enter focus is on the partner, and the second Enter adds no clip (0 → 0). There were no errors and no forbidden requests.
  - The first attempt timed out waiting for the library, most likely because the dev server reloaded after my edit. The next two attempts passed with identical results. Only the last run's files remain, because each run overwrote the previous one's.

**Code-reviewer** (score 8/10, nothing Critical; the three questions from B came back clear):
- **S1 (Medium), scrolling:** fixed as described above.
- **S2 (Medium), test gap:** added LF10. With the video floating, a focused ◀ click sends focus to ▶, not to ⤢ (video expand) and not to the body.
- **S3 (Low):** a click the parent refuses could leave the handoff armed. Today's parent always commits the change, so it can't happen; recorded for B.
- **S5 (Medium, new finding for B):**
  - **Repro:** while the video has the library temporarily open, focus ◀ or a library option and press Escape. Focus drops to the body, and the next Enter adds a clip (0 → 1).
  - **Why not fixed here:** this path goes through the frozen `StudioWorkspace.tsx` and never triggers this round's handoff.
  - **Pre-existing?** Based on the code path, yes. I did not re-run it in a browser against the snapshot.
  - **Evidence:** `a-round-110/probe/s5-probe-result.json`.
- **Architecture note (verbatim):**
  > There are now two copies of the arm-then-layout-effect focus handoff with a repeated-Enter guard (ArrangementTransport.tsx:78-107, ArrangementLibrary.tsx:173-231), and they differ in one structural way: Transport only hands off after confirming the action took effect (`source.disabled`), while the library checks nothing. Keep both inline for now, because extracting a helper before that difference is settled would bake one of the two behaviours into it. Proposal for the planner: a bounded task to add a `useFocusHandoffAfterCommit` hook plus a shared `preventRepeatedEnterKeyDown`, owned by `app/hooks/`, with a required "action took effect" check, migrating both callers with their existing tests (Transport's round-108 tests, library-focus-handoff, floating-video l.710-726, render-budget) passing unchanged.

**Next C checks:** LF-COLLAPSE, LF-EXPAND and LF-CLEAR (1280 and 1440), LF-MOUSE, LF-HOLD, LF-VIDEO-NEUTRAL, LF-SWEEP-NEG, R12-L2-ENTER-ADD, REG-LIB (also check that the panel's horizontal scroll stays 0 while ▶/◀ animate), FV-710, PX-NET, REG-HYD, G110-3, AN-REVIEW (re-run m1, m2 and m4 with C's own strings), T110-TARGETED (13 files), DOC-095 / DOC-094-L4, SOURCE-UNCHANGED.

Everything is in `/home/runner/czaba-project/tmp/studio-real-loop/`: the full report with every command is `a-round-110.md`, and the rest (summary JSON, end hashes, logs, probes, mutation results) is under `a-round-110/`.
